candidate.answerReason: The percentage condition yields (10 − x)(y + 11) = 110 with 1 ≤ 10 − x ≤ 9. Its three positive integer candidates are (9,99), (8,44), and (5,11); only the last is relatively prime.

methods.label: Turn the condition into a fixed product
methods.explanation:
A \(10\%\) increase multiplies the original value by \(11/10\), so the required condition is
\[
\frac{x+1}{y+1}=\frac{11x}{10y}.
\]
Since \(x,y\) are positive integers, both denominators are positive. Clearing them and collecting terms gives
\[
10y(x+1)=11x(y+1),
\]
\[
(10-x)y=11x.
\]
The right side is positive, so \(10-x>0\). Thus \(1\leq x\leq9\).

To use the integer restrictions, add \(11(10-x)\) to both sides. This produces the fixed product
\[
(10-x)(y+11)=110.
\]
Let \(m=10-x\). Then \(m\) is a positive divisor of \(110\) with \(1\leq m\leq9\). The only such divisors are \(1,2,5\), giving
\[
\begin{aligned}
m=1 &: \quad (x,y)=(9,99),\\
m=2 &: \quad (x,y)=(8,44),\\
m=5 &: \quad (x,y)=(5,11).
\end{aligned}
\]
The first two pairs have common factors \(9\) and \(4\), respectively. The pair \((5,11)\) is relatively prime, and it satisfies the original condition because
\[
\frac{5+1}{11+1}=\frac12
=\frac{11}{10}\cdot\frac5{11}.
\]
Every possible integer pair has been considered, so exactly \(\boxed{1}\) fraction qualifies, choice \(\text{B}\).
